deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): (r_ν) is an increasing sequence of positive reals tending to ∞, and n(r) = #{ν : r_ν ≤ r} is its counting function. Writing Σ r_ν^{-α} as the Stieltjes integral ∫ r^{-α} dn(r) and integrating by parts gives (1) and (1 bis): Σ_{r_ν<b} r_ν^{-α} = n(b−0)/b^α + α∫_0^b n(r) r^{-α-1} dr. From this Grothendieck proved Σ r_ν^{-α} < ∞ ⇔ ∫^∞ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr < ∞.

This page completes the proof that convergence forces n(r)/r^α → 0. Suppose n(b_i)/b_i^α > ε along b_i → ∞. Using the bound n(r) ≤ M r^α (the λ_i in the manuscript are the b_i), we get n(b_i) − n(b_{i−1}) ≥ ε b_i^α − M b_{i−1}^α. Hence the block sum over b_{i−1} < r_ν ≤ b_i of r_ν^{-α} is at least (n(b_i) − n(b_{i−1})) b_i^{-α} ≥ ε − M(b_{i−1}/b_i)^α. Passing to a sparse subsequence makes M(b_{i−1}/b_i)^α ≤ ε/2. Then infinitely many disjoint blocks each contribute ≥ ε/2, contradicting convergence. Letting b → ∞ in (1 bis) gives the full formula (2)/(1').

He then states the generalisation to a weight λ that is C^1 and decreasing on R^{+*}:
- Σ λ(r_ν) < ∞ ⇔ ∫_0^∞ n(r)(−λ'(r)) dr < ∞;
- in that case λ(r)n(r) → 0;
- and Σ_{r_ν>a} λ(r_ν) = −λ(a)n(a+0) + ∫_a^∞ n(r)(−λ'(r)) dr.
The last line is a crossed-out or unfinished finite version λ(b)n(b) − λ(a)n(a+0) + ....

Purpose (clear from the next page): r_ν will be the moduli of the zeros of an entire function f. Combining with Jensen's formula (V(r) = mean of log|f| on |z| = r) relates Σ λ(r_ν) to the growth of f. This is the classical link between the exponent of convergence of the zeros and the order or growth of the function (Borel, Lindelöf, Hadamard theory), presumably for use in functional-analytic or Fourier contexts in these 1953 notes.
errors: Notation slip: the points are called b_i in the hypothesis but λ_i in the inequalities (λ_i = b_i). The letter λ is also reused immediately afterwards for the weight function.
The bound n(r) ≤ M r^α used in the step is justified only on the previous page (and there in a partly crossed-out remark). It follows easily from n(r) r^{-α} ≤ Σ_{r_ν≤r} r_ν^{-α}.

In the general statement the condition 'et tendant vers zéro' appears struck out while 'décroissante' is inserted. Without λ → 0 the equivalence is false: for λ constant and positive the integral is 0 but the series diverges. One needs λ(∞) = 0, or else the formula picks up the term λ(∞)·(number of terms).
The final displayed line is incomplete or abandoned.

ideas.what: Abel/Stieltjes summation: Σ r_ν^{-α} converges iff ∫ n(r) r^{-α-1} dr converges, and then n(r) = o(r^α)
ideas.modern_name: Partial summation for counting functions; exponent of convergence of a sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Abel summation; Borel, Lindelöf in the theory of entire functions, c. 1900)
ideas.where_published: Not known in his published texts; standard textbook material (e.g. Boas, Levin, Titchmarsh)

ideas.what: Generalisation to a decreasing C^1 weight λ: Σ λ(r_ν) expressed as ∫ n(r)(−λ'(r)) dr
ideas.modern_name: Stieltjes integration by parts, ∫ λ dn = −∫ n dλ

ideas.what: Preparation for combining with Jensen's formula (next page) to bound sums over zeros of entire functions by the mean of log|f|
ideas.modern_name: Jensen formula / Nevanlinna counting function N(r)
ideas.where_published: Not known in his published texts

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical real-variable lemma (Abel summation for counting functions of zeros), written out as a student-style exercise. Nothing new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The λ_i in the inequalities should be read as b_i (or the author's slip for them): n(b_i) − n(b_{i−1}) ≥ ε b_i^α − M b_{i−1}^α.
'Si alors on fait b→∞ dans (1 bis)' — the manuscript reads roughly 'Si alors on fait b → ∞ dans (1 bis), on obtient (2)'; the label is hard to read.
In the last line the first term is likely λ(b)n(b−0), matching the next page.
